title: 社会学与人类学 Day 36：社会科学还能相信吗
title_en: Sociology & Anthropology Day 36: Can We Trust Social Science?

questions.question: 要比较两个国家居民的自评健康，怎样才能让「很好/好/一般/差」这类自评真正可比？
options: 把四档改成十档量表，选项越细，不同人勾选的含义就越一致
把问卷翻译得更准确，确保两国被试读到的选项字面意思完全一致
扩大样本量、把结果精确到小数点后更多位，统计误差变小了，数字自然就可比了
让所有人给同几个虚构人物打分，用打分差估出各人尺子的差别，再校正自评
questions.explanation: 喀拉拉与比哈尔的例子说明，报告「有病」取决于你把什么状态认作病，尺子长在本地、随经验漂移，不是谁在说谎。King 等人的修法是固定的虚构案例：大家对同一案例打分的差就是尺子的差。精度、译文和档位都不解决「是不是同一把尺子」。
questions.question_en: To compare self-rated health ('very good / good / fair / poor') across two countries, what makes such self-ratings genuinely comparable?
options_en: Replace the four categories with a ten-point scale, since finer options make everyone's ticks mean the same thing
Translate the questionnaire more carefully so both groups read options with exactly the same literal meaning
Enlarge the sample and report more decimal places; with smaller statistical error the numbers become comparable
Have everyone rate the same few fictional people, use the differences in those ratings to estimate each person's yardstick, and correct the self-ratings accordingly
questions.explanation_en: The Kerala–Bihar case shows that reporting illness depends on what you recognize as illness; the yardstick is local and drifts with experience, and nobody is lying. King and colleagues' fix uses fixed vignettes: differences in rating the same invented case are differences in yardsticks. Precision, translation and finer scales don't address whether people hold the same ruler.

questions.question: 「搬向机会」实验：2007 年的报告没发现成年人收入效应，2016 年追踪发现幼年搬家的孩子成年后收入高出三成。这组结果最该带走的教训是什么？
options: 只要随机化做得足够好，第一次测量就能给出最终答案，根本没有必要再做长期追踪
邻里效应确实被夸大了，2016 年的结果只是税务数据带来的偶然波动
2007 年的研究者读错了数据，抽签随机化在早期就出了问题
「效应」必须说清对谁、多久之后、量哪个结果，否则连能判对错的说法都不算
questions.explanation: 同一个实验、同一批人、随机化一点没变，变的只有量什么、量谁、隔多久量：成年人收入无效应，幼年搬家的孩子二十多年后收入显著更高，青少年时搬家的反而略负。这不是谁读错了，而是「效应」这个词本身不完整。
questions.question_en: In Moving to Opportunity, the 2007 report found no effect on adult earnings, while 2016 follow-up found children who moved young earned about 30% more as adults. What is the key lesson?
options_en: With good randomization, the first measurement gives the final answer and long-term follow-up is unnecessary
Neighbourhood effects really were overstated; the 2016 result is just noise from the tax data
The 2007 researchers misread the data, and the lottery randomization broke down early on
An 'effect' must specify for whom, how long afterwards and which outcome; otherwise it isn't even a claim that can be right or wrong
questions.explanation_en: Same experiment, same people, randomization untouched — only what was measured, on whom and when changed: no effect on adult earnings, a large gain for children who moved young, a slightly negative estimate for those who moved as teenagers. Nobody misread anything; the word 'effect' is simply incomplete on its own.

questions.question: WEIRD 问题的头号例子「木匠世界假说」（缪勒-莱尔错觉的跨文化差异）在 2025 年被重新审视后几乎站不住。这该怎么理解？
options: WEIRD 问题不因此为假：自我反省用的证据同样会错，反省也要被检验
木匠世界假说被推翻，恰恰证明视觉错觉完全由文化环境塑造
这说明跨文化研究整体不可信，心理学应当只研究本国样本以避免误差
WEIRD 问题原来是虚构的，心理学以西方大学生为样本得出的结论可以放心推广到全人类
questions.explanation: Amir 与 Firestone 发现这种错觉在动物、其他感官、先天失明者身上也出现，原始数据的跨文化相关也不一致。但这不推翻 WEIRD 问题：最后通牒博弈在十五个小社会里的差异才是更硬的证据。窄样本的坏处是不知道结论管到哪儿为止。
questions.question_en: The flagship example of the WEIRD problem — the 'carpentered world' explanation of cross-cultural differences in the Müller-Lyer illusion — was found in 2025 to be almost certainly wrong. How should this be read?
options_en: It doesn't make the WEIRD problem fake: a discipline examining itself uses equally fallible evidence, so the self-examination must be checked too, and stronger evidence lies elsewhere
Overturning the carpentered-world hypothesis proves that visual illusions are entirely shaped by cultural environment
It shows cross-cultural research as a whole is unreliable, so psychology should study only domestic samples
The WEIRD problem was imaginary, so findings from Western undergraduates can safely be generalized to all humans
questions.explanation_en: Amir and Firestone found the illusion in animals, in other senses and in congenitally blind people, and the original cross-cultural correlations were inconsistent. That doesn't overturn the WEIRD problem: the ultimatum-game differences across fifteen small-scale societies are firmer evidence. The harm of a narrow sample is not knowing how far a conclusion reaches.
